milestones.label: Campaign launch
milestones.detail: Platner enters the race for U.S. Senate in Maine.

milestones.label: First negative wave begins
milestones.detail: CNN KFile and Politico publish deleted-Reddit-posts stories the same day.

milestones.label: Tattoo preemption
milestones.detail: Told that tattoo images were being shopped as opposition research, Platner releases video via Pod Save America.

milestones.label: Mills suspends campaign
milestones.detail: Gov. Janet Mills suspends her primary campaign; her name stays on the ballot.

milestones.label: Pre-primary stories
milestones.detail: WSJ and NYT explicit-texts stories publish the same day — ten days before the primary.

milestones.label: NYT dating-history article
milestones.detail: “Several Women Who Dated Graham Platner Recall ‘Unsettling’ Behavior” — five days before the primary.

milestones.label: PRIMARY — Platner wins
milestones.detail: 156,084 votes, 72.13% of valid votes (official final); most primary votes of any Democratic U.S. Senate candidate in Maine history since 1918.

milestones.label: Assault allegation published
milestones.detail: Politico publishes Jenny Racicot's sexual-assault allegation; WaPo and CNN carry parallel interviews the same day.

milestones.label: Campaign suspension announced
milestones.detail: Platner posts video: “this is all false … we are suspending campaign operations.”

milestones.label: Formal withdrawal
milestones.detail: Written withdrawal filed with the Maine Secretary of State.

milestones.label: Statutory withdrawal deadline
milestones.detail: 5 p.m., second Monday in July — last day a primary winner's withdrawal lets the party fill the vacancy (21-A M.R.S. § 374-A).

milestones.label: Party replacement deadline
milestones.detail: 5 p.m., fourth Monday in July — deadline for the party committee to nominate a replacement.

milestones.label: General election
milestones.detail: The seat held by Sen. Susan Collins is on the ballot.

monthly_overlay.note: Stories = primary records in the media catalog (excludes secondary/aggregation items). Spending = FEC Schedule E independent expenditures by filing date, deduped (F24 notices double-filed on later F3X reports removed); support figures approximate for small undated items. Sources: attacks.json; outside-money FEC research (candidate ID S6ME00373).

series.note: Stronger America Inc. (501(c)(4)) reported giving $3M to Pine Tree Results PAC on 2025-12-29 — a donor into the PAC, not an FEC independent expenditure.
July stories run Jul 6–10; no new opposing IE filings in the Jul 1–8 window in the deduped ledger.

opponents.name: Janet T. Mills
opponents.note: suspended campaign Apr 30; remained on ballot

mandate.record: Most primary votes received by any Democratic U.S. Senate candidate in Maine history, since popular Senate elections began in 1918 (AP data / state election data analysis, reported by Maine Public, Jun 11, 2026).
mandate.record_caveat: The statement's broader claim — largest number in the history of Maine primaries, all offices and parties — is unverified.
mandate.election_night_note: Election-night partials showed 77.7% when the race was called (BDN, 9:07 p.m.); the official final tabulation is 72.13% of valid votes.
mandate.source: Maine Secretary of State, official final tabulation, US Senate DEM - FINAL.xlsx
